event_name: Victorian Christmas Candlelight Night at William Root House
blurb: The William Root House does one of the more quietly cool holiday events in the area on December 11th. Candlelit rooms decorated with live greens, fruit, and handmade pieces in full 1860s style, cooking demonstrations, and live music running from 4 to 8 PM. It's low-key in the best way. No massive crowds, no inflatable Santas, just a genuinely atmospheric evening in a historic house that reminds you what the holidays looked like before everything was electric and plastic. Good for a date night, good for empty nesters who want something with actual character. Worth the short drive to Marietta.
scoring_notes: Appeals to the educated, culturally curious segment of the Perimeter audience. Empty nesters and couples without kids will find this more appealing than families with young children, which fits the adult-skewing nature of this newsletter. The 1860s historical angle is genuinely differentiated from generic holiday events.

event_name: Taiwanese Winter Night Market Cooking Workshop
venue: Mise en Place Cooking Studio, Roswell
blurb: Taiwan's night markets are genuinely one of the great food experiences in the world, loud, crowded, smoky, and delicious in a way that's hard to replicate anywhere else. This workshop at Mise en Place Cooking Studio tries to bring that energy into a hands-on format on December 4th, which makes it a fun Friday night activity with a bit more substance than dinner and a movie. You're in Roswell, which is a quick shot up 400 from the Perimeter, and it runs 6 to 8:30 so the whole evening is still yours after. Good pick if you like to cook, good pick if you just want to eat well while learning something. Check Mise en Place for ticket pricing and availability.
scoring_notes: High-education, higher-income Perimeter audience maps well to experiential food and cooking events. Friday evening timing is ideal. Roswell is a reasonable distance from the Perimeter area. The Taiwanese night market theme is specific and culturally interesting rather than generic.

blurb: Black Friday night and you're looking for something to do that isn't more shopping. Here's your answer. Fetty Wap is at Coca-Cola Roxy on November 28th, and if you came up listening to Trap Queen on repeat in 2015, this one's going to hit different live. The Battery is an easy night out from the Perimeter, the venue is comfortable, and an 8 PM show means you can eat first without rushing. Grab tickets before they're gone and make it a proper night out.
scoring_notes: Median age of 38 puts this audience squarely in the demographic that knows Fetty Wap's catalog well. Black Friday timing is a genuine differentiator since most people are off work. The Battery location is convenient for Perimeter residents. Adult skew works for this newsletter's audience mix.

blurb: Tyla is one of the most exciting artists to break in the last few years, and Water alone put her on a global stage fast. She's at Coca-Cola Roxy on December 6th, and if you've been sleeping on seeing her live, this is a small enough room that you'll actually feel it rather than watching her as a dot on a stadium screen. South African Amapiano-influenced pop at that venue is going to be a different kind of Sunday night. Tickets are out there now, and this one will sell.
scoring_notes: Tyla skews slightly younger but her crossover appeal is broad. Perimeter's young professional demographic is a solid match. The Roxy is an intimate venue for an artist at her current level of visibility, which is a genuine selling point. Sunday show may limit attendance but that's a minor trade-off.

event_name: Sound of Music Sing-Along at The Strand
blurb: If you've ever hummed Do-Re-Mi while doing something completely unrelated to music, you already know why this is worth your Sunday. The Strand is screening the 1965 Sound of Music as a full sing-along, which means lyrics on screen, everyone participating, and zero judgment when you belt out Edelweiss louder than you planned to. Show up 30 minutes early for a live pre-show concert on the Mighty Allen Theatre Organ, which is a genuinely rare thing to hear in person. At just under three hours it's a full evening, and it's the kind of experience you can't replicate at home on a streaming service. Great for families, great for a date night if your person is the type who knows all the words.
scoring_notes: Sing-along format is a genuinely differentiated experience vs. a standard screening. The live organ pre-show is a rare touch that adds real value. Broad demographic appeal across young families and empty nesters. Marietta is a short drive from the Perimeter coverage zone.

event_name: Jason Bonham's Led Zeppelin Evening at Coca-Cola Roxy
blurb: Here's the thing about Jason Bonham's Led Zeppelin Evening: it's not a tribute band in the traditional sense. Jason is John Bonham's son, he toured with Led Zeppelin himself, and when he plays his father's parts he's playing them from memory, from the inside, the way you can only do when it was your house growing up. If you've got any affinity for Zeppelin's catalog, that context changes what you're watching. The Coca-Cola Roxy is a great room for this kind of show, close enough that you feel it, big enough that it still has energy. Thursday December 10th, 8 PM. Worth a weeknight.
scoring_notes: Led Zeppelin's core fanbase maps well to the 35-55 age range that makes up a significant portion of the Perimeter audience at median age 38. Jason Bonham's specific backstory gives this real uniqueness beyond a standard tribute act. Adult skew fits the newsletter well.

event_name: Chanukah Festival and Menorah Lighting at Vinings Jubilee
blurb: Vinings Jubilee is one of those spots that already feels like a neighborhood gathering place, and on December 6th it gets even better. Chabad of Smyrna is hosting a full Chanukah Festival around the Clocktower starting at 5:30 PM, and it's the kind of evening that works whether you're bringing kids or just want a reason to get outside on a Sunday. There's a menorah lighting, hands-on crafts, face painting, and seasonal treats. Free and open to everyone, no ticket required. RSVP through Chabad of Smyrna is encouraged so they can plan accordingly.
scoring_notes: Vinings sits on the southern edge of the Perimeter coverage area and pulls strongly from that audience. Family-friendly but short enough (2 hours) that it works for adults without kids too. Free price point is a genuine plus here because it lowers the barrier for a Sunday-night outing.

event_name: 6th Annual Dunwoody Village Menorah Lighting & Giant Gelt Drop
blurb: This one is literally in your backyard. The 6th Annual Dunwoody Village Menorah Lighting & Giant Gelt Drop is a full community event put on by Mitzvah House right at Dunwoody Village Pkwy, and it has all the right ingredients for a weeknight that actually feels festive. Rabbi G leads songs, the DHS Band plays, there are donuts and latkes (yes, both), and then the Giant Gelt Drop happens, which, if you've never seen it, is exactly as chaotic and fun as it sounds. The game truck is a nice touch if you're bringing kids. Free, open to everyone, and you don't have to drive far. RSVP ahead so they have a headcount.
scoring_notes: Dunwoody is squarely in the Perimeter coverage zone. Free community event with broad appeal across young families and young professionals. Chanukah timing makes it seasonally unique this week. The Giant Gelt Drop is a genuinely fun hook that differentiates it from a standard menorah lighting.
